clue.text: Tied to a railway line

blocks.note: tied up means bound
taken as written
RY is the standard abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Someone or something lashed to the tracks, like a villain's victim in an old silent film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Railway line' looks like one unit, but 'line' is split off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A boundary is the dividing mark between two areas, such as a border drawn on a map.

clue.text: Some rhubarb is tropical in this restaurant

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of the run of letters is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A menu oddity: a restaurant serving rhubarb as if it were a tropical fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal eatery in the French style.

clue.text: Remove spell of good fortune when sitting on one's bottom

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sitting on another is placed above it

blocks.note: an up, as in ups and downs, is a lucky period
the root of something is its base or bottom

explanation.surface: A lucky streak dispelled as soon as someone sits down on their backside.
explanation.definitionFit: To uproot is to pull a plant out of the ground, so to take away or dislodge.

clue.text: Mechanical excavator, one from down under

blocks.note: first meaning: a machine that excavates earth
second meaning: an Australian or New Zealander, especially a soldier

explanation.walkthrough: Down under is Australia and New Zealand; their soldiers in the First World War were nicknamed this.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a machine for excavating ground and, as slang, an Australian person.

clue.text: River's colour helps you spot imitation diamond

blocks.note: the Rhine is a major European river, with possessive S
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: Advice to a jeweller: the stone's colour tells you whether a diamond is fake.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhinestone is a paste gem of glass or crystal, made to look like a real diamond.

clue.text: Followers found in coach or train

blocks.note: first meaning: a group of disciples sharing one master's ideas
second meaning: a verb, to teach or drill someone

explanation.surface: Fans or followers turning up aboard a bus or a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach and train look like vehicles, but here they are verbs meaning to instruct.
explanation.definitionFit: A school of painters or thinkers is a band of adherents; to school someone is to educate or drill them.

clue.text: Little Caroline's outside silver coach

indicators.note: one piece placed outside another wraps around it

blocks.note: Carrie is a pet form of the name Caroline
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A little girl standing beside a silver coach, like a fairy-tale princess.
explanation.definitionFit: A carriage is a horse-drawn coach or a railway passenger car.

clue.text: Conventional hot rod free to steer

indicators.note: set free, the letters break loose from their order
to here means added on to, joining the two pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
a steer is a castrated bullock, an ox

explanation.surface: A modified hot rod car being free to drive however one likes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb about driving; it is the noun for a young bullock.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodox means following accepted, traditional rules and beliefs.

clue.text: Noel looks stupid and a little rejected

indicators.note: something that looks stupid is in a silly state, so the name's letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
some means a small amount

explanation.surface: A man called Noel feeling foolish and somewhat spurned.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lonesome feels solitary and forlorn, as if cast off by others.

clue.text: Lots of women changing gears and oil when reversing

indicators.note: changing the word's letters puts them in a different order
reversing a word means reading it from its last letter back to its first

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mechanic's job: changing the gears and the oil while backing the car up.
explanation.walkthrough: The seraglio is the women's quarters of a Turkish palace, and by extension the women living there.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is a harem, a household housing many wives and concubines of a sultan.

clue.text: Nectar befuddled this Greek islander

indicators.note: a befuddled mind is muddled, so the word's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek islander made tipsy by sweet drink, as if on the nectar of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Crete, the largest Greek island, is called by this demonym.

clue.text: O swan, embraced by broken reed! Undone again!

indicators.note: something embraced sits inside the arms of what holds it, and a broken word is split apart to hold it

blocks.note: taken as written
a pen is a female swan
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mock-poetic lament, apostrophising a swan among broken reeds by a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The reed is broken in two so that the other letters can sit in its middle. The female swan is a pen, the male a cob.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reopened has been unfastened or opened a second time after being shut.

clue.text: Addicted to Chianti, perhaps: it makes common sense after six

indicators.note: after says which piece comes second when the two are joined end to end

blocks.note: six in Roman numerals
nous is a British word for practical good sense

explanation.surface: A wine-lover's defence: knocking back Chianti makes perfect sense after six in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinous means relating to or fond of wine, and Chianti is an example of a red wine.

clue.text: It's smashing here, if you have courage when on the shelf

indicators.note: in a down entry, being on something means placed above it

blocks.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
a bank is a raised shelf of sand or earth, as under the sea

explanation.surface: A spinster cheered on: life on the shelf can be smashing if you have courage.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottle bank is a public container for recycling glass, where bottles are dropped in and break.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass dropped into a recycling bin shatters, so it is a place where smashing happens, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Determined to have scope in the bank, perhaps

blocks.note: strong-willed means determined
room to manoeuvre is scope

explanation.surface: An ambitious bank employee resolved to be given more scope at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a place found in the bank, perhaps, rather than a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongroom is the secure vault where a bank keeps cash and valuables, though other buildings have them too.

clue.text: Small child gets stuck into, preferably, a glass of sherry

indicators.note: stuck into means pushed inside another word

blocks.note: CH is the short form of child
sooner, as in I'd sooner not, means rather

explanation.surface: A toddler tucking into a drink, preferably sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' signals that child is cut to its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a tall stemmed glass used for serving sherry.

clue.text: One in small house takes care of unfinished regatta, when capsized

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its ending, so its last letter goes
a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down entry the word runs bottom to top

blocks.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
taken as written

explanation.surface: A villager in a little home looking after an abandoned regatta whose boat has overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottager is someone living in a cottage, a modest rural dwelling.

clue.text: Affiliation to political party, say, had altered with a stand-up row

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters take a new order
standing up in a down entry turns the word to read upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a row is a loud noise or din

explanation.surface: A party member whose loyalty shifted after a furious stand-up argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand-up row' reads as a heated quarrel; stand-up is the reversal signal and row is noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesion is steady attachment or loyal support, as to a cause, belief or party.

clue.text: Harmonise fancy decoration

indicators.note: fancy suggests something elaborately reworked, so the word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An interior designer's instruction to make the ornate decor match.
explanation.definitionFit: To coordinate colours or parts is to make them work together and match each other.

clue.text: Indoor morning headgear for crowd getting better

indicators.note: getting means acquiring, so the second piece is added on

blocks.note: a mob is an unruly crowd
to cap a story is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: Choosing hats for a throng whose mood is improving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective but is the verb meaning to top or outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobcap is a soft frilled cotton bonnet once worn by women indoors.

clue.text: Contrarily, Evita demands name from mother

indicators.note: contrarily means the opposite way, so the name runs backwards
demanding something means asking for it to be put in place, here ahead

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eva Peron, the musical's heroine, stubbornly insisting on being named after her mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Native qualities are inborn, acquired at birth, as with a mother tongue or mother country.

clue.text: Anyone for this bouncing fault reaching the net?

indicators.note: reaching means getting as far as, so one piece is joined to the next
a bouncing ball comes back, so the letters go upwards in this down entry

blocks.note: a sin is a moral fault
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ball bouncing up to clip the net on a court, the cry of an amateur match.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the stock phrase 'Anyone for tennis?' from drawing-room comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase invites people to play a racket game, so 'this' stands for that game.

clue.text: Escape in old hat, an obstruction

blocks.note: something old hat is out of fashion
a let is a hindrance, as in the legal phrase without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: Someone fleeing in a battered old hat, hampered by an obstacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like a garment but means outdated. Let as an obstruction survives in law and in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlet is a vent or way out through which something escapes, such as water or feelings.

clue.text: Bare backdrop seen in time

indicators.note: seen in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: drop means lose, and back reads it the other way round
a date is a point in time

explanation.surface: A stage set's backdrop on view at a particular period; a theatre note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backdrop' reads as one theatrical word but splits into a reversal signal and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A desolate landscape is barren and empty, stripped of life or comfort.

clue.text: Any number going round in one's head

indicators.note: going round suggests turning and churning, so the word's letters are mixed

blocks.note: N is the algebraic symbol for an unspecified number
taken as written

explanation.surface: Numbers swirling around inside someone's head, like a mind full of figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Noggin is informal slang for the head, as in use your noggin.

clue.text: Authorise the Jewish religion round a new court

indicators.note: round means wrapped around, so the following letters sit inside

blocks.note: Sion is a variant spelling of Zion, the Jewish people and faith
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A religious authority approving a new court of law.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction an action is to give it official permission or approval.

clue.text: Eager artist joins a circle

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A keen painter signing up to an artistic circle.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Raring, as in raring to go, means very keen and impatient to start.

clue.text: Sea captains wanting second breakfast

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
kippers are smoked herrings, a traditional British breakfast

explanation.surface: Hungry ship's masters asking for a second helping at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second breakfast' reads as a second helping; second is just the abbreviation S, and kippers (smoked herrings) are the breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the master of a ship or boat, so plural skippers are captains at sea.
